pr.title: Carry a published summary forward through project summary refresh
pr.head: d5fa6673eac7204d107c99a639a14f6a00b92b0d

summary: A summary is the JSON file behind a pull request's guided review page on the Projector site. project summary publish stores each one on the hidden ref refs/projector/summaries, in a folder per pull request and head. When a pull request moves, an agent updates the summary it published before rather than writing a new one.

Until now that update was done by hand. The summarize-pr skill told agents to fetch the ref, find the newest folder with git log, copy its summary.json out with git show, and edit the JSON: set pr.head, move new files into groups, and drop files that left the diff. Nothing told agents to update pr.base, the merge base the page's diff starts from. After a pull request merged its base branch, the stale base pulled the base's own changes into the diff, and validate then demanded groups for files the pull request never touched.
This pull request adds two commands so an agent writes only the prose and chooses the groups:

• project summary init --from-published copies the pull request's newest stored summary instead of writing a skeleton. It picks and dates the newest head the way the site does, and --head picks one head instead.
  • project summary refresh resets every pr field from GitHub, pr.base included, adds files new to the diff to the unassigned group, drops files that left the diff and prints their prose, and lists notes whose line the new diff no longer shows.
The skills and docs now run these two commands in place of the hand-edit steps.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• Summaries ref: refs/projector/summaries, a hidden ref (not a branch) holding summaries/<number>/<head>/summary.json for every published head.
  • Tracking ref: this checkout's copy of the remote's summaries ref, at refs/projector/remotes/origin/summaries.
  • spec.json: the name an older release stored summaries under. The site reads only summary.json, but dates a republished head by its spec.json.
  • Walkthroughs ref: refs/projector/walkthroughs, the ref's name before summaries were renamed.
  • unassigned group: the group init puts every file in, for the author to sort into real groups.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html:
Projector's review of d5fa667 found no defects and posted no finding threads. It suggested one optional change: refresh prints full 40-character SHAs for pr.head and pr.base, while the docs example shows them shortened. The full test suite, project check, and both plugin validations pass at this head.

Left for later: project summary migrate, which would delete the old walkthroughs ref once every site reads the new one.

groups.title: Refreshing a summary to the current head
groups.kicker: project summary refresh and the helpers it shares with init and validate
intro: refresh reads a summary file, asks GitHub for the pull request's current pr fields and diff, and rewrites the parts of the summary a program can decide. carry_forward does the work in memory and returns what it changed, and refresh writes the file and prints a report.

1. Every pr field is replaced. The summary's pr becomes exactly what pr_metadata returns, so pr.base follows a merged base branch, and pr.basePr, the pull request this one is stacked on, disappears when it is no longer stacked.
  2. Files that left the diff are dropped from their groups, and their note and checks are printed so the author can move what still applies.
  3. Files new to the diff join the unassigned group, which is created last when the summary has none.
  4. Notes on lines the new diff does not show are listed and left in place. validate refuses such notes, so the author must move them before publishing.
The file is rewritten only when a pr field changed or a file was added or dropped, and it is replaced in one step so a reader never finds it half written.

checks.text: A group the drops empty is reported but kept. validate accepts an empty group, so the summary still validates until the author removes it or moves files into it.

files.note: Adds carry_forward and refresh, and factors current_diff, unassigned_group, write_summary and file_row out of init so both commands share them. validate's line check moves into unshown_lines, which refresh also uses to find stale notes.

checks.text: The change lines print each value whole, so pr.head and pr.base appear as full 40-character SHAs. Every other line of the report shortens a head to nine characters, and the docs/cli.md example shows them shortened. The review left this as an optional suggestion.
Replacing pr outright, rather than merging into it, is what removes basePr once the pull request is no longer stacked. Any other key a summary carried in pr goes too and is reported as → none.

A file is new when no group still lists it after the drops, so a file already in a group is never added twice. test_new_files_join_the_unassigned_group_the_summary_has checks that an existing unassigned group is reused rather than duplicated.
When nothing changed, the file is not rewritten: test_a_summary_already_at_the_head_is_left_alone compares the inode and modification time before and after a second run.
validate reports the same lines through unshown_lines and side_of as its inline check did before. The check still treats a missing or unknown side as new, and still flags a non-integer line.

groups.title: Copying the newest published summary
groups.kicker: project summary init --from-published, and the ref reading it shares with site serve
intro: init --from-published copies a stored summary to the --summary path instead of writing a skeleton. It checks that the remote is the repository --repo names, fetches the remote's summaries ref into the tracking ref, and picks a head with newest_summary. If the fetch fails, it says so and reads the copy the checkout already has.
The choice must match what the site shows as the pull request's newest summary, so it reuses the ref reading that project site serve already does:

• Which refs: summaries_refs gives the tracking ref and this checkout's own refs/projector/summaries, or the walkthroughs ref when neither exists.
  • Which date: a head is as new as the commit that last changed its spec.json when it has one, and its summary.json otherwise. So republishing an old head, which adds a fresh summary.json beside its old spec.json, never makes it outrank a newer head.
  • Ties: when both refs date their newest alike, this checkout's ref wins, as it does on the site.
commit_times, split out of extract_summaries, gives the date of each path for both callers.

files.note: Adds newest_summary and StoredSummary, and splits commit_times out of extract_summaries so both date summaries the same way.

checks.text: A head stored only as spec.json is a candidate here, though the site leaves such heads out. That lets --head copy one for republishing, as docs/site.md now describes.

Heads with the same date keep the first one found, in the path order ls-tree lists, which matches the site's stable sort over a sorted list of paths. The walkthroughs history keeps its dates when it is carried over, because seed_from_legacy replays each commit with its original dates.

files.note: Adds the --from-published, --remote and --head options to summary init, the summary refresh subcommand, and init_from_published, which runs the copy.

checks.text: A remote whose URL is not a GitHub URL, such as a local path, gives an empty slug and skips this check.
The fetch writes only the tracking ref, never FETCH_HEAD, so it is safe in a checkout that other sessions also fetch into.
--remote or --head without --from-published, and --diff with it, exit with a usage error; test_the_published_summary_options_need_each_other covers all three.

groups.title: Tests
groups.kicker: Fourteen tests against temporary Git repositories and a stubbed gh
intro: FromPublishedTests stores summaries on a local bare remote with chosen commit dates and runs init --from-published through the CLI. RefreshTests stubs gh with a pull request whose base was merged in, so one file moved, one left the diff, and one joined it.

files.note: Covers newest-head selection, republished old heads, spec.json-only heads, the walkthroughs ref, a summary kept in the checkout, ties between refs, --head, nothing stored, a mismatched remote, usage errors, and each part of refresh.

groups.title: Skills and documentation
groups.kicker: Every by-hand read of the summaries ref now runs the new commands
intro: The summarize-pr skill's "Update the page when the pull request moves" flow now runs init --from-published, then refresh, then the agent's prose edits. Every other place that told an agent to read the ref by hand, including reading another stack layer's project and republishing a spec.json head, now uses init --from-published.
In review-pr, only the "Update rather than start over" bullet changed. docs/cli.md documents both commands.

checks.text: Agents follow SKILL.md files as instructions, so read the two skill files as behavior changes, not prose.

files.note: Replaces the git fetch and git show steps with init --from-published, adds refresh as the first step of an update, and renumbers the steps after it.
The review loop's summary step now runs init --from-published first and updates what it finds.
Drops the advice to keep pr fields when editing by hand, and says refresh resets them.
Documents init --from-published and refresh, with an example of refresh's output.
The steps for republishing a spec.json head use init --from-published --head in place of git show FETCH_HEAD:….
